sentences.text: Malawisuchus is an extinct genus of notosuchian mesoeucrocodylian found in the Early Cretaceous Dinosaur Beds of Malawi.
This small crocodilian reached a length of about 60 centimetres, or 24 inches.
It possessed unusual, mammal-like teeth, including those with multiple cusps at the rear of the jaw.
Elizabeth Gomani formally described Malawisuchus in 1997 as a member of the family Notosuchidae.
The type species M. mwakasyungutiensis is named after Mwakasyunguti, the area in northern Malawi where the fossils were discovered.
The jaw joint suggests it processed food using a forward motion.
Strong neck and hind legs suggest an upright posture and ability to run, while upper arm muscles indicate it could dig.
The preservation of articulated specimens suggests Malawisuchus lived in or was preserved within burrows.
Carvalho and colleagues reclassified Malawisuchus as a member of the family Itasuchidae in 2004.
The Paleobi Database lists the parent group of Malawisuchus as Candidodontidae.
Malawisuchus lived during the Aptian stage, between 121.4 and 113.2 million years ago.
